  PUBLIC PARTICIPATION AND ACCESSIBILITY
  PLEASE SILENCE CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION

Viewing of City Council Meetings:
  • In-person – City Council Chambers, 613 E. Broadway, 2nd Floor, Glendale, CA 91206
  • Live Broadcast via Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-verse,
  channel 99. Meetings are also streamed on the City webpage, glendaleca.gov/live, on
  YouTube.com/myglendale, and on the Cablecast app under "Glendale TV". Meetings are also
  archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas.
City Council meeting agenda packets, any agenda related documents, and additional documents
are available at City Hall and online for public viewing on the City’s website:
https://www.glendaleca.gov/government/public-meeting-portal

ADA Accessibility and Translation Services:
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. The City Clerk’ office should be notified 72 hours (three
business days) or as soon as practicable for requests regarding sign language translation and
Braille transcription services; please direct all accessibility requests to (818) 548-2090. For
translations, please specify the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of
City provided interpreters is not required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or
speak in their native language.

Public participation in Council meetings may occur as follows:
  • In-person – City Council Chambers
  • Telephonic participation: Call (818) 937-8100
If you have any questions about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance including
agenda email notification, please contact the City Clerk’s Office via email at
CityClerk@GlendaleCA.gov, or by phone at (818) 548-2090.

   PUBLIC COMMENT GUIDELINES
The City Council welcomes public input at City Council meetings. Public input at Council meetings
is regulated by the City Council’s Rules of Order, Procedure and Decorum for the Conduct of City
Council Meetings as set forth in Resolution No. 25-76, which will be summarized below.

Written Comments and Documents:
Public comments received in writing will NOT be read aloud at the meeting but will be part of the
meeting record. Written public comments can be emailed to citycouncil@glendaleca.gov, and will
be uploaded to the City website as an attachment to the agenda item. When submitting a public
comment, please make sure to include the following:
  1. Name (optional); and
  2. Agenda item to which you are submitting public comment
  3. Submit no later than 12:00 p.m. on the day of the City Council meeting. Correspondence
  received after this time may not be distributed until the following business day.
All documents related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours
prior to this meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City
Clerk, 613 E. Broadway, Room 110, Glendale, CA 91206.

Public Comments During Council Meeting:
Public Comments during Community Event Announcements, First and Second Periods of Oral
Communications and agenda items will be governed as provided in the descriptions for those items
on the agenda below. Pursuant to State law, the City Council may not discuss or take action on any
item not appearing on the meeting agenda, except that members of the City Council or staff may
ask a question for clarification or briefly respond to statements made or questions posed by
persons exercising public testimony rights (Government Code Section 54954.2). Staff may be
asked to follow up on such items.

Submitting Speaker Cards or Calling In for Public Comment:
Speaker cards must be submitted and telephonic participants must call in and be in the call-in
queue as follows:
  • Community Event Announcements or First or Second Period of Oral Communications: PRIOR
  TO the commencement of the specific comment period
  • Consent Calendar Items: BEFORE a motion is made on the consent calendar
  • Other agenda items, including Action items: PRIOR to the completion of the verbal staff report
  (unless waived by the Mayor)
Any audio-visual files displayed by speakers must be emailed to the Clerk’s office by 12:00 pm on
the day before a Council meeting.

5.  CITY COUNCILISTAFF COMMENTS (Including reports from conferences and

  City Clerk Dr. Abajian made a presentation regarding the California Statewide
  Special Election taking place on November 4, 2025. She shared that there are
  eight Vote-by-Mail Ballot Drop Boxes in Glendale, located at the Glendale
  Central Library, Wilson Mini Park, Pacific Park Library, Verdugo Park,
  Grandview Branch Library, Glendale Sports Complex, Dunsmore Park, and
  Montrose-Crescenta Branch Library. All Ballot Drop Boxes in Glendale are open
  24 hours. She also highlighted two City Vote Centers located at the Glendale
  Civic Center (141 N. Glendale Ave., Room 118, Glendale, CA 91206) and the
  Chevy Chase Branch Library (3301 E. Chevy Chase Dr., Main Room, Glendale,
  CA 91206). Hours for both locations are as follows: November 1—3, 10:00 AM to
  7:00 PM, and November 4, 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM.

  2

 Councilmember Asatryan shared that AB 91 was signed into law by Governor
Newsom, which will add checkboxes for Armenians and various other minority
communities on all California state forms. She thanked the joint authors of the
bill, Assemblymember Harabedian and Senator Perez, as well as co-authors
Assemblymembers Nick Schultz and Jessica Caloza, the California MENA
Coalition and all the advocates, particularly Dr. Abajian and Dr. Sophia Armen,
for their leadership in getting this bill passed. She announced that this Saturday,
October 11, 2025, from 10:30 AM to 12:30 PM, will be the official Grand
Reopening of Fremont Park. She also shared that on Sunday, October 12,
2025, the 8th Annual Wine Festival Ginifest” will take place from 3:00 PM to
9:00 PM at the 200 N. Orange Block, and that this year it will be expanded into
a street festival.

Councilmember Brotman requested that two items be agendized. The first
relates to Zone Zero, and he requested staff from the Fire Department and
Urban Forestry Division to bring back a joint report regarding Zone Zero and its
potential impact on Glendale. Ultimately, he would like Council to consider
submitting a letter to the Board of Forestry expressing the City’s views on the
proposed rules. The second item concerns complaints from various
neighborhoods about excessive speeding leading to dangerous conditions for
pedestrians, motorists, and parked cars. He asked staff to prepare a report on
plans and ideas to address this issue, including enforcement measures and
long-term solutions. Mayor Pro Tem Kassakhian added that he has additional
locations of excessive speeding he would like to include in Councilmember
Brotman’s list.

Councilmember Gharpetian shared comments on events he attended, including
the National Foundation Day of Korea celebration, the Circle Society of
Glendale Gala, and the Lark Music Center Grand Opening. He requested that
City Attorney Mike Garcia follow up with him regarding a previous motion he
made about costs resulting from state mandates. He also expressed interest in
bringing back the Unity Fest to Glendale. Finally, he asked City Manager
Roubik Golanian whether the Council had sent a letter to the State opposing AB
130. City Manager Golanian confirmed that the Council voted to send the letter,
which was signed by Mayor Najarian. Councilmember Asatryan clarified that the
Sister Cities Committee is currently working on an event similar to the Unity
Fest.

 Mayor Pro Tern Kassakhian cornrnented that Oktoberfest was well attended
and congratulated the organizers. He also remarked on the Glendale Historical
Society Gala and thanked Councilmernber Gharpetian for presenting
commendations on behalf of Mayor Najarian at the Lark Center Opening,
congratulating the Board as well. He shared that the Armenian Bone Marrow
 Donor Registry held a successful Walk-A-Thon. He also announced that on
Saturday, October 11,2025, from 10:30AM to 12:30 PM, the official Grand
Reopening and Ribbon Cutting of Fremont Park will take place. That same day,
from 5:00 PM to 6:00 PM, the Jewel City Concert Series at Artsakh Paseo will
feature the Indie Pop/R&B group The Guest Room. Later, from 6:00 PM to 9:00
PM, the Brand Library will host an exhibition opening and reception titled
Crossings. He noted that next Tuesday, October 14, 2025, there will be no
regular City Council meeting, as the “City Hall in Your Neighborhood” event will
take place at the Sparr Heights Community Center (1613 Glencoe Way,
Glendale, CA 91208) at 6:00 PM. He also mentioned that information about the
Alex Theatre’s 100th Anniversary programming can be found at
www.thealex.com. Additionally, he shared that Little Bear, an Italian restaurant,
will hold its Grand Opening from 4:00 PM to 8:00 PM at 6800 San Fernando
Rd., though he will not be attending as he will be at the League of California
Cities Conference. Lastly, he requested to agendize a discussion about
regulating robot delivery units in Glendale, as well as enforcement related to A-
frame sign regulations.

City Attorney Michael Garcia responded to Councilmember Gharpetian’s
questions, stating that his staff is reviewing the issue and plans to provide an
update by next week.
